item.title: Reddit Moves to a Logged-In Only Experience, With Tests in Select Markets Outside the US (2026)
item.description:
Reddit will become a "logged-in only experience," CEO Steve Huffman announced on the platform and during the company's third-quarter 2026 investor call.

Testing starts in select markets outside the US in the coming months, and Reddit plans to roll the change out globally afterward. Huffman says the move is meant to protect Reddit's data from unauthorized scraping, which mostly happens through logged-out access, and to personalize the site for people who sign in.

The announcement follows a sharp drop in search traffic. Reddit lost an average of one million search engine referrals per week in October, according to Huffman, who said that "Google has really shifted in their relationship with the rest of the internet."

What Changes for Logged-Out Reddit Visitors

Reddit has not published a full list of what logged-out users will still be able to see. Huffman did name exceptions. He said "the front page being available logged-out is useful and important," and that Reddit wants people to be able to share posts, with visitors arriving from search or other external sources still seeing the content they were linked to.

Everything else points toward accounts. Huffman described joining communities, voting, commenting, and participating as "fundamental to the Reddit experience," and said logged-in users let Reddit personalize feeds and "surface what's most relevant." The company states that more than 80% of its revenue already comes from logged-in and app users.

Data access is the other driver. "Access to Reddit's data corpus has to be intentional," Huffman said, adding that "the vast majority of unauthorized access to Reddit" happens through logged-out experiences.

Reddit currently has AI training arrangements with OpenAI and Google, and Huffman said the company is in "active discussions" about those deals without announcing changes. Discord recently took the opposite direction when it decided to make discoverable server messages searchable on Google.

Options for Users Who Browse Reddit Without an Account

Creating a Reddit account requires an email address, a username, and a password. No phone number is needed. For users who want to browse without tying activity to their account, Reddit says it has rebuilt its privacy-focused incognito mode in the app and is releasing it again. Huffman describes the mode as read-only and "truly private," meaning browsing and searches do not affect the logged-in account.

  1. Check whether the logged-out front page and shared links still load in the region once testing begins.
  2. Create an account with an email address if regular access to subreddits is needed.
  3. Switch on incognito mode in the Reddit app for read-only browsing that stays separate from the main account.

Reddit reported 53% year-over-year revenue growth and 16% growth in weekly active users for the third quarter, but its share price dropped after the company issued a lower-than-expected forecast. Reddit has not named the markets where testing will begin or given a date for the global switch.

item.title: OpenAI Doubles ChatGPT Pro and Business Premium Usage Limits After Dropping a Planned Pro 200 Cut (2026)
item.description:
OpenAI has doubled usage limits for its $100, $200, and $500 ChatGPT Pro plans and for Business Premium, effective October 29. The announcement came from Tibo, who represents ChatGPT and Codex on X, and it replaces an earlier plan to reduce the usage allowance for existing Pro 200 subscribers after October 29.

"We are doubling all usage limits for all Pro 100/200/500 tiers and Business Premium, effective today," Tibo wrote. The company says it reversed course following customer feedback.

OpenAI Reverses the Planned ChatGPT Pro 200 Usage Cut

OpenAI had planned to lower the included usage allowance for Pro 200 subscribers while keeping the subscription price at $200 per month. That cut is now off the table. "We heard your kind feedback and won't be reducing usage limits for Pro 200, so your Work and Codex usage will stay the same," Tibo said in the same post.

The higher limits mainly affect ChatGPT Work and Codex, which share usage allowances under eligible subscriptions. Pro subscribers who rely on Codex for coding tasks or on Work for longer jobs get more room before they hit the cap, without moving to a more expensive tier.

OpenAI is also keeping extended limits for Dots, its always-on AI assistants. "We're also going to continue offering extended limits for Dots for now, and usage of your dot will still continue to be separate from your default usage," the company said. Dots usage therefore does not draw from the doubled Work and Codex allowance.

The change follows a busy month for OpenAI pricing, including the launch of GPT-6.1 Terra with lower API pricing earlier this week.

What ChatGPT Pro and Business Premium Subscribers Should Check

No action is required to receive the higher limits, since OpenAI applied them to eligible accounts immediately. Subscribers can still use the change to review their plans:

  • Pro 200 subscribers who were preparing to switch plans because of the announced cut keep their previous Work and Codex usage, now doubled.
  • Pro 100 subscribers who regularly reach their cap get twice the allowance at the same $100 price.
  • Pro 500 and Business Premium customers receive the same doubling on their existing allowance.
  • Dots users keep a separate allowance that does not count against default usage.

OpenAI does not publish exact numerical usage limits for each tier, so subscribers cannot verify the doubling against a published figure. The company also describes the extended Dots limits as available "for now" and has not said how long they will stay in place.

Thank you for being a Ghacks reader. The post OpenAI Doubles ChatGPT Pro and Business Premium Usage Limits After Dropping a Planned Pro 200 Cut appeared first on gHacks.

item.title: Football Manager 27 Is Free to Play on Steam Until November 3 Ahead of Its November 10 Launch (2026)
item.description:
Football Manager 27 is free to play on Steam until November 3 at 10 am PT (1 pm ET) as part of the Steam Free Weekend promotion, ahead of the game's official release on November 10.

The free period gives players the full Launch Preview of the latest entry in the soccer management series from Sports Interactive and SEGA, and progress carries over to the full game.

Unlike a typical Steam demo, the Football Manager 27 Launch Preview is the complete game. Some bugs and missing assets may still be present because the build predates the official launch.

Football Manager 27 Free Weekend Details and Launch Discount

Players lose access when the free period ends on November 3. Football Manager 27 then gets a launch discount on Steam that runs through the official release date of November 10, so players who decide to buy after the preview can keep their saves and continue with the club they started.

Football Manager 27 puts players in charge of a club, from signing players and developing talent to making decisions that change matches. The new entry adds:

  • an improved Tactical Effectiveness system
  • more opportunities to adjust strategies during matches
  • enhanced stadiums and crowds
  • improved player animations

The free weekend is a full preview rather than a time-limited trial of selected modes, which makes it a practical way to check performance and the new tactical tools on a specific PC before paying for the game.

  1. Open the Football Manager 27 page in the Steam client or the Steam store.
  2. Install the game and start the Launch Preview before November 3 at 10 am PT.
  3. Decide whether to buy before the launch discount ends on November 10, if the save should carry over to the full release.

Hexologic Is Free to Keep on Steam Until October 31

Steam is also running a Free-to-Keep promotion this week. Hexologic, a 2018 puzzle game from indie developer MythicOwl, can be added to a Steam library at no cost and kept permanently if it is claimed before October 31 at 10 am PT (1 pm ET).

Hexologic puts a spin on Sudoku: players place dots inside hexagonal tiles so that their combined values match the numbers along the edges of each grid. The game has more than 90 levels across 6 worlds, and 96% of its 700 Steam reviews are positive, which gives it an "Overwhelmingly Positive" rating.

Football Manager 27 access ends with the free weekend on November 3, while Hexologic stays in the library only for users who claim it before the October 31 deadline.

Thank you for being a Ghacks reader. The post Football Manager 27 Is Free to Play on Steam Until November 3 Ahead of Its November 10 Launch appeared first on gHacks.

item.title: VGW, Blitz and Dabble gambling recovery suits stay in federal court (2026)
item.description:
Georgia Gambling Recovery LLC's lawsuits against Blitz Studios Inc., VGW Holdings Ltd and affiliates, and Dabble Sports LLC and affiliates will remain in federal court following an October 28, 2026 order by U.S. District Judge Clay D. Land. The Middle District of Georgia judge denied requests to return the three cases to state court. VGW is the group behind Chumba Casino. The ruling concerns where the cases will be heard, leaving the underlying gambling-loss claims unresolved.

Why the judge rejected the return to state court

According to the order, the company brought claims under Georgia's gambling-loss recovery statute, O.C.G.A. Section 13-8-3, over losses allegedly suffered by Georgia residents. The action began in the State Court of Muscogee County before defendants' cases were separated and transferred to federal court through removal.

Land found that the cases qualified for diversity jurisdiction, which allows federal courts to hear certain disputes between parties with different citizenship. Under 28 U.S.C. Section 1332(a), the amount in controversy must exceed $75,000, excluding interest and costs. The company challenged the basis for keeping these cases in federal court on three grounds.

First, it argued that Georgia was the true party pursuing the recovery claims. Land rejected that interpretation: the invoked statute did not authorize the company to pursue a claim belonging to the state. He held that the LLC itself was the real party in interest, defeating that objection to diversity jurisdiction.

Second, the company argued that removal was barred because the state court had separated the cases against its wishes. Land found no abuse of discretion in that severance and no available immediate appeal on this record. The separation therefore did not prevent removal.

Third, it argued that defendants' earlier challenge to its standing under the Georgia Constitution should prevent removal. Land rejected that argument because the state court had refused to accept the defendants' position. That earlier, unsuccessful challenge did not bar them from moving the cases to federal court.

What the order means for the recovery claims

The ruling awards no damages and does not decide whether the defendants violated gambling laws. The $75,000 threshold concerns federal jurisdiction; it is neither a confirmed total of player losses nor an amount awarded to anyone. The order establishes no customer refund procedure or payment deadline.

The claimant is a private LLC seeking recovery of alleged losses. This is not an enforcement action brought by Georgia's attorney general or a regulator. The VGW case docket separately identifies VGW Malta Ltd, VGW Luckyland Inc. doing business as Luckyland Slots, and VGW GP Ltd alongside VGW Holdings Ltd.

Although Land addressed all three remand requests in one order, he did not combine the cases into a single proceeding. The company had also asked for consolidation in its briefing. Land said that request required a separate motion so the defendants would have an opportunity to respond.

Thank you for being a Ghacks reader. The post VGW, Blitz and Dabble gambling recovery suits stay in federal court appeared first on gHacks.

item.title: Microsoft Fixes Windows 11 Always On VPN Failures From September Updates in KB5127936 (2026)
item.description:
Microsoft has fixed the Always On VPN connection failures that the September 2026 security updates caused on Windows 11, according to the release notes of the KB5127936 preview update.

The fix is available now on devices that install the optional October preview update for Windows 11 25H2 and 26H2. Devices that skip it stay affected until next month's Patch Tuesday cumulative updates.

The confirmation follows an earlier misstep. Microsoft had marked the issue as resolved in the October 2026 cumulative updates, then reopened the Always On VPN bug when it turned out the problem was still there.

Always On VPN Fix in KB5127936 and Affected Configurations

Microsoft first acknowledged the problem in a service alert sent to IT administrators in late September. According to that alert, the failures hit Windows 11 systems after the September security updates when Always On VPN profiles used automatic protocol selection with IKEv2 and SSTP.

The KB5127936 release notes describe the symptoms in more detail. "When automatic protocol selection or protocol fallback was configured, affected VPN connections could remain stuck in a Connecting state or fail to connect after an initial connection attempt failed," Microsoft says. In some cases, later connection attempts displayed the error "The specified port is already in use."

Always On VPN runs in the background and establishes secure tunnels back to a corporate network whenever a device connects to the internet. The remote access solution replaced the legacy DirectAccess technology and supports domain-joined, non-domain-joined, and Microsoft Entra ID joined devices running Windows 10, Windows 11, and Windows Server.

How Administrators Can Apply the Fix or Mitigate the Issue

Organizations have two paths. They can deploy the preview update now, or they can apply the temporary mitigation Microsoft published and wait for the November cumulative update.

  1. Install KB5127936 on affected Windows 11 25H2 and 26H2 devices through Windows Update or the organization's update management tool.
  2. If the preview update is not an option, open the Always On VPN profile and change it from automatic protocol selection to a single protocol.
  3. Pick SSTP only or IKEv2 only. Microsoft says organizations should select the protocol based on their environment, security, and deployment requirements.

The mitigation removes the protocol fallback that automatic selection provides, so admins who choose it should revert the profile once the fixed cumulative update is installed.

KB5127936 also resolves a separate known issue. Non-admin users could not connect to devices through Remote Desktop when the Administrator protection security feature was enabled after the September 2026 non-security preview update or later Windows updates.

Microsoft has not said whether the November Patch Tuesday release will include further changes to the VPN fix beyond what ships in KB5127936.

item.title: Google Confirms a Fix Is Coming for Pixel Watch Battery Drain Reported on Pixel Watch 2 to 5 (2026)
item.description:
Google has confirmed that it identified a battery drain issue on Pixel Watch smartwatches and is working on a fix, according to a statement the company posted in owner threads on Reddit. Owner reports cover the Pixel Watch 2, Pixel Watch 3, Pixel Watch 4, and the current Pixel Watch 5. Google has not given a release date for the fix.

"We have identified a battery drain issue, affecting a small number of Pixel Watch users, and are working to roll out a fix as soon as possible," Google says in its reply. "Thank you for your patience and understanding."

Pixel Watch Battery Drain Symptoms Across Four Generations

Complaints started earlier this week. On affected watches, battery life that normally lasts a day or two dropped to about 12 hours, and the drain continued even while the devices sat idle.

Turning off the Always-on Display did not make a noticeable difference for affected owners. Some reported an improvement after a full device reset, but that result was not consistent from one report to the next.

Google's statement does not list affected models. The model range comes from owner reports, and because those reports span four generations of hardware, a shared hardware failure is an unlikely explanation.

Google has not confirmed the cause, which software version introduced the drain, or the number of affected watches, beyond describing the group as "a small number" of users.

How Pixel Watch Owners Can Handle the Drain Until the Fix Arrives

Google has not published an official workaround. Owners who see unusually short battery life can take these steps while they wait:

  1. Check for system updates on the watch and update the Pixel Watch app on the paired phone, so the fix installs as soon as Google releases it.
  2. Compare battery behavior with the reported symptoms, especially heavy drain while the watch sits idle, to confirm the problem matches this issue and not normal heavy use.
  3. Leave the Always-on Display setting as it is if the only goal is fixing the drain, since disabling it did not help affected owners.
  4. Treat a full factory reset as a last resort. Some owners saw an improvement after resetting, but the result was inconsistent, and a reset means setting the watch up again from scratch.

The battery problem affects a product line where a day or two of battery life is the expected baseline, so a drop to roughly 12 hours makes affected watches hard to rely on through a full day.

Google has not shared a timeline beyond "as soon as possible," and the company has not said whether the fix will arrive as a watch system update or through an app update.

Thank you for being a Ghacks reader. The post Google Confirms a Fix Is Coming for Pixel Watch Battery Drain Reported on Pixel Watch 2 to 5 appeared first on gHacks.

item.title: Google Launches Gemini 4 Carbon for Cyber Defenders First, With API Pricing From $2 per Million Tokens (2026)
item.description:
Google has announced Gemini 4 Carbon, which the company describes as its most capable AI model for long-horizon tasks, in a post on the Google blog on October 28. Access starts with a subset of cyber defenders this week. Developers, businesses, and consumers cannot use the model yet.

Gemini 4 Carbon arrives two weeks after Gemini 4 Argon. Google says that in internal testing, Carbon worked on engineering tasks for days, pushing through roadblocks to diagnose, root-cause, and patch subtle bugs across large codebases.

Gemini 4 Carbon Benchmarks and API Pricing

Google reports that Carbon ranks first on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0 with a score of 59. On WebDev Arena, the model gained 89 Elo points to reach 1768, which places it fourth.

Cybersecurity is the focus of the launch. Google lists these scores:

  • SEC-bench Pro, which measures autonomous discovery of real-world vulnerabilities: 88.2%
  • ExploitGym, which tests whether discovered flaws can be exploited: 54.8%

item.title: Activision Will Remove Seoul Crowd Crush Footage From Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 on November 12 (2026)
item.description:
Activision will remove real-world footage of the 2022 Seoul Halloween crowd crush from the opening cinematic of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, the publisher said in a statement that also apologized to the families of the victims. The edit arrives in a game update scheduled for November 12, so the current cinematic stays in the game until then.

The crowd crush happened in October 2022 during Halloween celebrations in Seoul's Itaewon neighborhood. A surge in the narrow streets and alleys killed 160 people and left nearly 200 more injured.

Modern Warfare 4 uses video from that disaster in its opening to portray the immediate aftermath of a fictional North Korean invasion of South Korea, the premise of the game's story.

Activision Responds to Complaints From Victims' Families

Activision first said the footage was not meant to "reference or trivialize" the actual event and was used only "to establish the game's fictional narrative." Families of the victims rejected that explanation. In their statement, they called the use of the event in an entertainment product "highly inappropriate and senseless."

The families also said that if Activision "has even a minimum of courtesy and empathy towards the victims, it should take corrective action without delay." The publisher has now done that, a clear change from its first response, which defended the footage as part of the fictional setup.

"We offer our deepest condolences and sincere apologies to the bereaved families, victims and everyone who has been deeply hurt or distressed by this incident," Activision said in its latest statement.

Modern Warfare 4 Cinematic Update Timing for Players

The announced change covers the opening cinematic only. Activision has not said that any other campaign content will be edited, and the statement does not describe what will replace the removed clips.

Players do not need to take any action. The edited cinematic will arrive with the November 12 update through the normal patch process, and anyone who replays the campaign opening after that date will see the revised version.

The change comes during the launch window of a release that peaked at 227,434 concurrent Steam players, so the original version of the opening has been in front of a sizable player base since launch. The footage remains in the game on all versions until the update installs.

Activision has not published patch notes for the November 12 update yet, so the full scope of that release beyond the cinematic change is not known.

item.title: Microsoft Confirms Windows 11 Will Not Get Drag-to-Move Taskbar Support (2026)
item.description:
Microsoft has confirmed that Windows 11 will not let users drag the taskbar to move it to another edge of the screen, a behavior Windows 10 supported. Diego Baca, Vice President of Design at Microsoft, explained the decision in a post on X and described it as "a deliberate design decision, not a missing capability."

Windows 11 gained the ability to change the taskbar position earlier this year, but only through the Settings app. Baca's statement makes clear that Microsoft does not plan to add the drag gesture on top of that option.

Why Microsoft Kept Taskbar Positioning in Settings

Baca says Microsoft's research showed that dragging the taskbar to reposition it can lead to accidental movements. He points out that this risk is one of the reasons the "Lock the taskbar" option existed in earlier versions of Windows.

Microsoft also found that people rarely change the taskbar position. Most users pick a location once and leave it there, so the company decided that a setting reachable with a single right-click is the more predictable approach. Baca calls the result more intentional than a free drag gesture.

The workflow differs noticeably between the two versions:

  • Windows 10: right-click the taskbar, uncheck "Lock the taskbar", then drag the bar to the desired edge of the screen.
  • Windows 11: right-click the taskbar, open the taskbar options in Settings, then select the desired position from the list.

Resizing the taskbar by dragging its top edge, which Windows 10 also allowed, is not part of Windows 11 either. Microsoft's statement addresses only the drag-to-move behavior and does not mention resizing.

How to Change the Taskbar Position on Windows 11

Users who want to move the taskbar now have one route, the Settings app. The process takes a few clicks:

  1. Right-click an empty area of the Windows 11 taskbar.
  2. Open the taskbar settings from the context menu, which launches the Settings app.
  3. Pick the new taskbar position from the available options.

Because the bar cannot be dragged, the old lock option has no job left to do, which is the accidental-movement problem Baca describes. The trade-off is speed: users who switch positions often now go through Settings each time instead of grabbing the bar with the mouse.

Microsoft has adjusted other basic Windows 11 interactions recently, including the faster, customizable context menu in KB5127936. Baca's explanation was posted on X rather than in official Windows documentation, and Microsoft has not published the research data behind the decision.

item.title: Anthropic Adds a Claude Code Rule on Opus 5.5 That Blocks Recreations of Existing Games (2026)
item.description:
Anthropic has added a rule to Claude Code, its AI coding assistant, that stops the tool from recreating specific existing video games when it runs on the Opus 5.5 model.

Anthropic confirmed the change through a post by Addy Osmani, a member of its technical staff, who said the company added two sentences to Claude Code's prompt on Opus 5.5 to steer it away from rebuilding someone else's game.

The rule reached Claude Code around October 27, according to X user Chasm, who first shared the change. Chasm reports that the instruction is delivered from Anthropic's servers under a flag named "tengu_heron_brook" and that users cannot switch it off.

What the New Claude Code Rule Allows and Blocks

The instruction tells Claude to keep building original games, games in an established genre, and games based on the user's own designs and assets. Recreating a specific existing game is off the table, and the rule says this applies "even if it is renamed or called original."

In practice, the rule draws this line:

  • allowed: original game concepts, genre games, and projects built from the developer's own designs and assets
  • blocked: a copy of a specific existing game, including versions that carry a new name or are described as original

Osmani says the reason is Anthropic's usage policy, which already prohibits using Claude to infringe intellectual property. The prompt change makes Claude Code enforce that policy directly when a request targets a particular game.

Anthropic says it will continue to adjust the rule to strike the right balance. Osmani asked developers whose own projects are refused by Claude to send those cases to him directly.

Why Anthropic Is Targeting AI Game Clones

The change follows complaints about low-effort AI-generated games during Valve's Steam Next Fest in October. Players reported that their feeds filled up with clones of existing games, including copies of titles that had only just released their own demos.

Some developers reacted by pulling public demos. The team behind Drunken Goddess Reflux, Alliance Arts and Who You, canceled its Steam demo plans in favor of private playtests. Valve responded that it would be "thinking about how to solve this problem."

For developers who use Claude Code, the practical impact depends on the project. Original work and genre games should continue to work as before. Requests to reproduce a known game, or to rebuild one under a new title, now fail on Opus 5.5. Anthropic's previous Claude launch, the Claude Duet background agent, was limited to paying subscribers, while the game rule is applied server-side to Claude Code on Opus 5.5 with no user setting to disable it.

Anthropic has not said whether a specific incident prompted the change, whether the rule will extend to other Claude models, or how it treats mods, decompilations, and recompilations of existing games.

item.title: Android SMS of Death Exploit Goes Public, Leaving Android 12 and 13 Phones Without a Fix (2026)
item.description:
A security researcher has published a working exploit for an Android flaw dubbed "SMS of Death" that can crash phones and cut cellular service with a single crafted text message.

Google fixed the bug, tracked as CVE-2026-58882, in the October 2026 Android security updates for Android 14 through 17, according to researcher Mark Blah, while Android 12 and 13 devices did not receive the fix.

The attack is zero-click. Android processes the malicious message before it reaches the SMS inbox, so the target sees nothing that explains the crash. Blah notes that the flaw is not listed in Google's October security bulletin, even though the fix appears in Android's telephony code.

How the Android SMS of Death Attack Works

Blah traced the flaw to improper validation of a header-length value in Android's WapPushOverSms.decodeWapPdu function. An attacker sends a malformed eight-byte WAP Push message as a data SMS to port 2948. Without a bounds check, the length value turns into -2147483648 when read as a signed 32-bit integer.

Android then tries to allocate memory with that negative size, which throws a NegativeArraySizeException and crashes the com.android.phone process. Because that process manages cellular functions, the crash disrupts mobile connectivity and drops calls in progress, including calls to emergency services.

The damage can repeat. Carriers may try to redeliver the message, and Android may process messages already stored on the phone again. In Blah's testing, 20 malicious messages pushed phones into reboot loops. One Android 12 device restarted into recovery mode roughly every 90 seconds, and only a factory reset recovered it.

A GitHub contributor named Sakis found a way to remove the messages with Android Debug Bridge (ADB), but the method requires a computer and technical knowledge.

Blah has also released a proof-of-concept exploit that sends the malicious messages from another Android device, so the attack no longer requires custom tooling.

What Android Users Should Check Now

Google's fix, titled "Fix remote DoS in decodeWapPdu," catches the exceptions caused by the malformed messages and deletes those messages from the SMS database so they cannot trigger repeated crashes. Android owners can take these steps:

  1. Check the phone for a pending system or security update and install it.
  2. Restart the device if prompted, since installation may require a reboot to complete.
  3. Confirm that the phone runs Android 14 or later with the October 2026 security update or newer.

Security updates install automatically on supported devices, but availability depends on the phone maker and the carrier, so the timing of the October patch varies from one Android 14 to 17 phone to the next.

Owners of Android 12 and Android 13 phones have no patch to install. The October bulletin does not list CVE-2026-58882, and no fix for those two versions has been released.

item.title: Blizzard Plans World of Warcraft: Forever Content Updates Every Four Months After November 4 Launch (2026)
item.description:
Blizzard plans to release major content updates for World of Warcraft: Forever roughly once every four months, principal game designer Kris Zierhut said in an interview ahead of the game's November 4 launch. Zierhut described the schedule as "a little more laid back" than the cadence of modern World of Warcraft, in line with the slower pace of the new gaming project.

WoW: Forever is set in the original era of the MMO and keeps its slower travel, questing, and combat. Unlike each version of WoW Classic, it can draw on all of World of Warcraft's history for new content, which lets Blizzard keep updating it indefinitely.

World of Warcraft: Forever Update Schedule

Zierhut says the team experimented to find the right release rate and settled on something close to once every four months, or 17 weeks, which works out to three major updates per year.

The schedule is a reaction to Season of Discovery, the limited-time mode in which members of the same team shipped new content every eight to 10 weeks. Zierhut says that pace "felt way, way, way too fast."

The plan for WoW: Forever updates includes these elements:

  • major updates timed around new raid tiers, giving players months to work through each one
  • new activities for characters below the level cap, not only endgame raid content
  • parts of each update unlocking one, two, or three months after release through a timed event calendar

Zierhut says the staggered unlocks are meant to avoid a single content dump on patch day followed by four quiet months. The event calendar opens new things gradually across the update window.

How WoW: Forever Compares With Retail World of Warcraft

Retail World of Warcraft follows a faster rhythm. The current Midnight expansion released its 12.0.0 update in January and 12.1.0 in August, with interim content arriving roughly every three months in between. Retail WoW also uses expansions, while WoW: Forever is designed around horizontal progression without expansions.

For players deciding where to spend their time, the difference is practical. A four-month raid cycle gives guilds and casual players longer to finish content before the next tier arrives, and the timed unlocks spread smaller additions across that window instead of front-loading them.

Blizzard also says one of its goals is to "unsolve" the game, so that optimized routes and guides do not exhaust it quickly.

WoW: Forever launches on November 4. Zierhut did not give a date for the first major content update, and the four-month cadence is a target the team described rather than a fixed calendar.

item.title: Oklahoma sweepstakes casino ban takes effect, reaching suppliers and affiliates (2026)
item.description:
Oklahoma's SB 1589 took effect on November 1, 2026, bringing covered dual-currency online casino games and specified supporting businesses within the state's gambling prohibition. The enrolled legislation reaches beyond operators to name technology providers, gaming suppliers, promoters and media affiliates, extending criminal exposure to businesses that support the covered games.

The felony provision covers paid and unpaid support

The amendment to 21 O.S. Section 941 defines online casino games as internet-accessed gambling games in which a person risks a representative of value. That value definition expressly includes currency used in a dual-currency system that permits exchange for prizes, cash, cash equivalents or a chance to win them.

The support provision names owners or employees, geolocation providers, gaming suppliers, platform providers, promoters and media affiliates. It applies whether or not they are paid for dealing or providing support for those engaged in a covered game. The offense is a Class C2 felony, punishable upon conviction by a $500 to $2,000 fine and imprisonment under the cross-referenced sentencing provision.

The law preserves exceptions under the Oklahoma Charity Games Act and for gaming otherwise authorized on Indian lands in compliance with the federal Indian Gaming Regulatory Act.

The official bill history records a May 7 veto followed by overrides in both chambers on May 14: 34 to 10 in the Senate and 68 to 19 in the House.

Existing balances remain an operator-specific question

SB 1589 provides no special prize-redemption grace period and sets no process for resolving existing customer balances or pending requests. Its November 1 commencement therefore does not establish whether a particular operator will approve or deliver a prize requested before its access restriction.

Current NoLimitCoins terms limit Oklahoma access to Gold Coins mode, while Funrize's terms allow access in Tournament Points mode only. These are published availability conditions; they do not establish when either Oklahoma restriction first took effect or how an individual account is being handled.

For existing customers, continued access to an entertainment mode does not establish whether a previous prize request will be processed. item.title: Microsoft Removes PC-to-PC Migration From Windows 11 and Points Users to OneDrive-Based Windows Backup (2026)
item.description:
Microsoft has removed the PC-to-PC Migration feature from Windows 11, according to an updated Microsoft support page that now states the tool is no longer available.

The removal started with the September optional update (KB5124010) and reached regular users through the October 13, 2026 Patch Tuesday update, KB5127648.

Microsoft's support documentation now redirects users to Windows Backup, a tool that relies on OneDrive cloud storage instead of a direct connection between two computers. The company has not explained why the local transfer option was pulled.

What Windows 11 Users Lose With PC-to-PC Migration Gone

PC-to-PC Migration arrived in 2025 as a modern replacement for Easy Transfer from the Windows 7 era. The feature moved files and settings directly between two PCs over Wi-Fi or Ethernet. Users paired the old and new computer with a one-time code, picked the folders to copy, and Windows handled the rest.

It was never a full system migration tool. Installed apps, saved passwords, sign-in information and some protected folders stayed behind. For setting up a replacement computer, though, it moved files between drives and folders without any cloud account or storage quota involved.

Windows Backup works differently. It requires a personal Microsoft account and backs up supported folders (Desktop, Documents, Pictures, Videos and Music) to OneDrive.

Free OneDrive accounts include only 5GB of storage, and Microsoft's own promotional screenshot for Windows Backup shows 4.5GB of that allowance already in use. Years of photos, documents and downloads can exceed the free tier quickly.

Windows Backup does carry some extras. It can remember installed apps, Wi-Fi networks, passwords and some settings to speed up setup on a new device. Apps still have to be reinstalled, and supported files are restored from the cloud.

How to Move Files to a New Windows 11 PC Now

Users replacing a computer have three routes after the KB5127648 update:

  1. Use Windows Backup with a personal Microsoft account and check the OneDrive storage quota first, since free accounts stop at 5GB.
  2. Copy files manually with a USB drive or external storage device, moving the user folders to the new PC by hand.
  3. Use a network share on the local network to transfer folders between the old and new computer without cloud storage.

The manual methods avoid the OneDrive requirement and the 5GB storage limit. They take more effort, and Windows does not guide users through them the way PC-to-PC Migration did, so the folder selection is left to the user.

Microsoft has not said whether a local migration option will return to Windows 11, and the support page offers no alternative beyond Windows Backup.

item.title: Google Says a Fix Is Rolling Out for Android Auto Connection Problems on Samsung Phones With One UI 9 (2026)
item.description:
Google says an update is rolling out to fix Android Auto connection problems affecting Samsung Galaxy phones that have installed the One UI 9 update. A Google spokesperson confirmed on November 2, 2026 that the fix is being delivered and that the issue should be resolved soon. Google had earlier acknowledged the problem in a response to a submission on the Android Auto Help page.

The connection failures surfaced as One UI 9, Samsung's latest Android update, continues to reach additional Galaxy devices each week.

Android Auto Problems Reported After the One UI 9 Update

Owners of Galaxy phones running One UI 9 report three types of Android Auto failures:

  • random disconnects from the car's head unit during a drive
  • phones that fail to connect to Android Auto at all
  • audio stuttering that some users say has become worse since the update

The problem is not limited to a single Samsung model. User reports point to a wide range of Galaxy handsets that have received One UI 9, so owners of older and current models alike can run into the disconnects.

One UI 9 has already had one major bug, which Samsung has since fixed. The Android Auto issue is the second notable problem tied to the update, and Google, rather than Samsung, is the company delivering the fix in this case.

What Galaxy Owners Should Do Until the Fix Arrives

Google has not said which app or component the fix ships in, so the practical steps are limited to what drivers can check on their own:

  1. Install pending app updates on the phone so the Google fix is applied as soon as it reaches the device.
  2. Watch for disconnects or audio stuttering in Android Auto after updating to One UI 9, and report the behavior through the Android Auto Help page, where Google has already responded to submissions about the problem.
  3. Galaxy owners who have not installed One UI 9 yet and depend on Android Auto daily can wait for the Google fix to arrive before updating.

One UI 9 also brings expanded Quick Settings customization that lets users shrink and expand widgets, so postponing the update means waiting longer for those features.

The One UI 9 rollout is still in progress, and not all eligible Galaxy devices have received it. Google has not provided a timeline for when the Android Auto fix will reach every affected phone.

item.title: Phantom Blade Zero Sells 4 Million Copies in 72 Hours, Peaking at 833,921 Concurrent Steam Players (2026)
item.description:
Phantom Blade Zero has sold 4 million copies within 72 hours of going on sale, developer S-Game announced through the game's official X account. The wuxia action game is available on Steam, PlayStation 5 and Tencent's WeGame storefront, and its Steam player count peaked on Sunday at 833,921 concurrent players.

S-Game, the studio behind the game, shared the milestone only days after release as the title held first place in the Steam charts for gaming sales. "Thank you everyone from the bottom of our hearts for all the love and support!" S-Game wrote in the announcement post.

Phantom Blade Zero Tops Steam Charts at Launch

Phantom Blade Zero moved to the top of the Steam charts as soon as it launched, ahead of long-running titles such as PUBG and Dota 2. The game was also the best-selling title on Steam by revenue, finishing ahead of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, Aion 2 and Probably Stolen, a cyberpunk shopkeeper simulator.

The result tops recent Steam launches covered here, including Modern Warfare 4's 227,434 player Steam peak, which Phantom Blade Zero has now passed by more than 600,000 concurrent players.

Demand was visible before release. Estimates published last week put Phantom Blade Zero above 1 million copies sold before launch across Steam, PS5 and WeGame. Nearly two thirds of those prelaunch sales came from China, Taiwan and Hong Kong.

The launch still trails Black Myth: Wukong, which sold 10 million copies in its first three days. S-Game has not released a regional breakdown of the 4 million figure or split it by platform.

Phantom Blade Zero Cast and Availability

Roger Craig Smith, known for voicing Sonic the Hedgehog, Ezio Auditore and Chris Redfield, plays Soul, the lead character. Maggie Robertson, who played Lady Dimitrescu in Resident Evil 7, voices Mu Xiaokui. Donnie Yen served as a key creative consultant and plays Mó Yuan, Soul's father, through full facial, voice and motion capture.

Players interested in the game have three storefronts to choose from:

  • Steam on PC, where the game holds the top revenue spot
  • PlayStation 5 through the PlayStation Store
  • WeGame, Tencent's PC storefront in China

Steam players can verify the concurrent player figures on the game's Steam charts listing, which tracked the 833,921 peak on Sunday.

S-Game has not shared a sales target for Phantom Blade Zero beyond the 4 million milestone, and the game remains limited to Steam, PS5 and WeGame at launch.

item.title: Anthropic's Revised IPO Filing Reports $33.2 Billion in Nine-Month Revenue and $895 Billion in Compute Commitments (2026)
item.description:
Anthropic reported revenue of $33.2 billion for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, according to a revised IPO prospectus the AI company filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on Monday.

The amended S-1 filing also lists nearly $895 billion in compute and infrastructure commitments, and additional estimated payments could push Anthropic's total compute tab beyond $1 trillion.

The figure represents a year-over-year growth rate of 1,206%, the filing states. Anthropic warns in the same document that it does not expect revenue to keep growing at comparable rates and "cannot assure you that it will continue to grow at all."

Anthropic Revenue Growth Slows in the Third Quarter

The revised filing shows quarterly growth already easing. Revenue rose nearly 2.5 times between the first and second quarter of 2026. Third quarter revenue of nearly $17 billion was up 46% from the second quarter, while compute and infrastructure costs climbed 77% over the same period.

Cloud marketplaces accounted for roughly 44% of Anthropic's revenue in the nine months ended September 30. Anthropic says no single customer accounts for more than 10% of revenue.

The filing still treats reliance on hyperscalers for distribution as a risk, since Amazon, Google and Microsoft either build competing products or offer models from Anthropic's rivals.

Anthropic Compute Commitments Approach $1 Trillion

The prospectus puts Anthropic's commitments at about $895 billion, up from the more than $800 billion reported a week earlier. The breakdown in the filing:

  • roughly $320 billion in existing contractual obligations
  • about $451 billion in signed leases that have not commenced yet
  • nearly $70 billion in contractual payments due by September 2027
  • around $447.5 billion in commitments expected to be incurred by the end of 2030

Anthropic separately estimates additional payments made to secure adequate compute at $150 billion to $175 billion, which brings the total above $1 trillion. Deals with Microsoft, Google, Amazon and Broadcom now total $437 billion and are non-cancellable, and some require payment whether or not Anthropic uses the capacity. Of the $895 billion in contracts, only about $213 billion allow Anthropic to avoid payments.

"Our ability to meet the substantial and growing financial obligations of these requirements to secure compute depends on our ability to generate significant revenue growth," the filing reads. Debt or equity financing remain options, but leaning on them long term could dilute existing shareholders or force borrowing on unfavorable terms.

For Claude users and API customers, the filing does not announce any product or pricing changes. Anthropic expects the signed leases to begin between 2026 and 2028, and some of those agreements remain subject to termination rights or other conditions.

item.title: Google Says K-12 Students at Schools That Turn Off Its AI Tools Will Lose Google Search (2026)
item.description:
Google will switch off access to Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Google Search for K-12 student accounts until school administrators explicitly turn them on, the company announced in a blog post titled "Designing responsible AI for learning."

Chris Phillips, Google's vice president and general manager of education, has confirmed that students at schools that keep Google's AI tools turned off will not have access to Google Search either.

"After listening to schools, teachers, leading researchers, and policymakers, we are now updating our approach to controls for Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Google Search," Phillips wrote. Google presents the change as a way to ensure that "schools should have control over AI in their classrooms."

Why Google Ties Search to Gemini for Student Accounts

The link comes from Guided Learning, a Gemini mode that coaches students through problems with open-ended questions and step-by-step breakdowns. Google says its research shows Guided Learning produces measurable learning gains, and the company is bringing the mode to Google Search and Google Classroom.

Phillips said in an interview that "search and AI are deeply integrated." Students at schools that disable the AI tools "will not have access to search, and they'll see a message from their school that indicates it's not available," he said.

For school IT administrators, the update leaves one decision point with these outcomes:

  1. Leaving the controls off keeps Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and Gemini in Classroom unavailable to K-12 students, and Google Search stays off with them.
  2. Turning the tools on restores Google Search for student accounts, with Guided Learning built in to help students work through problems without skipping straight to answers.
  3. Enabling Search on its own still brings AI along, because Google is building Guided Learning into Search for all student accounts.

Teachers' Union and Critics Respond to Google's Policy

American Federation of Teachers president Randi Weingarten said that "Google has prioritized its business interests over the education of our children." Fairplay, a non-profit that campaigns against marketing to children, said Google's "attempt to strong-arm schools into using its AI products is likely to backfire." The group urged schools to turn off the AI tools and look for privacy-protective search alternatives.

Former FTC chair Lina Khan accused Google of "using its search monopoly to coerce schools into adopting AI," pointing out on X that multiple courts have found the company liable for violating antitrust laws. New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani said that "Google is trying to use its monopoly power to force AI into our public schools."

The policy arrives days after Alphabet shares fell sharply as AI Mode cut into Google's search business. Google has not said when the updated controls take effect for existing student accounts.

item.title: Google Bans Videostrong After Its Backdoor Turned 1.3 Million Android TV Boxes Into the XCPE Botnet (2026)
item.description:
Google has disrupted the XCPE botnet, a network of more than 1.3 million Android TV streaming boxes, and banned Chinese manufacturer Videostrong Technology Co. from producing certified Android devices, according to a report published Monday by the Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG). Google says Videostrong deliberately built the backdoor into devices it manufactured and sold access to criminal affiliates.

"We assess with high confidence that the backdoor and botnet were intentionally developed, deployed, and operated for financial gain by Videostrong Technology Co.," GTIG said.

Google also took down command-and-control servers used by more than a dozen related malware families, cutting off access to at least 10 million additional compromised devices. Those include retail set-top boxes, karaoke machines, and telehealth hardware, and Google says not all of them run Android.

Google Revokes Videostrong's Android TV License

Google has ended its relationship with Videostrong and revoked the company's license to manufacture Android TV devices with preloaded Google apps and services.

The ban extends to future affiliates, which cannot produce certified Android devices or supply software to certified vendors. Google says it changed its certification review process after finding that Videostrong used obfuscation to evade security testing and load malicious code only after a device first booted.

Japan's National Police Agency joined the operation alongside security companies Lumen, HUMAN Security, Plume, Synthient, and TrendAI. Synthient traced the backdoor to Videostrong after finding it preinstalled on a MECOOL KM9PRO Max Android TV box bought in late 2025, and the researchers found Videostrong company email addresses had been used to sign the backdoors.

XCPE did not arrive through a vulnerability or a malicious download. The malware, tracked as x.cpe and com.oemservice, sat in the firmware from the factory and ran with Android system-level privileges. Operators could use it to:

  • silently download and install additional Android apps
  • disable Google Play Protect
  • run shell commands and scripts with system privileges
  • capture screenshots and inject keystrokes
  • collect account information, device details, installed app lists, and system logs

Affiliates used the boxes for ad fraud, ran residential proxy software that routed third-party traffic through owners' connections without consent, and installed further backdoors named Moyu, Spirit, and Bird.

What Owners of Infected Android TV Boxes Can Do

The takedown disrupted XCPE's operations but did not remove the malware from infected boxes, Google says. The backdoor reinstalls itself from the /oem/ partition when it is deleted, so removing the malicious apps alone does not clean a device. Owners of affected boxes have two options:

  1. Install clean firmware on the box to remove the infection.
  2. Disconnect the box from the internet to stop further malicious activity if clean firmware is not available.

Google says Videostrong placed the malware in different device brands and models over multiple years, but the company has not published a full list of affected products beyond the MECOOL box identified by Synthient.

The takedown disrupted XCPE's operations but did not remove the malware from infected boxes, Google says. The backdoor reinstalls itself from the /oem/ partition when it is deleted, so removing the malicious apps alone does not clean a device. Owners of affected boxes have two options:

item.title: Microsoft Says Windows 11 26H2 Makes 8 GB PCs Up to 20% More Responsive and 40% Faster at Multitasking (2026)
item.description:
Microsoft has detailed a set of memory management changes in Windows 11 that it says make PCs with 8 GB of RAM up to 20 percent more responsive and 40 percent faster at multitasking, according to a Windows Experience Blog post by Pavan Davuluri, executive vice president of Windows and Devices. The improvements ship in Windows 11 26H2, build 26300.9818 or later.

The post follows a renewed push on memory optimization that Microsoft started earlier in 2026. Copilot+ PCs, which Microsoft continues to promote, require at least 16 GB of RAM, while memory prices keep climbing on demand from AI infrastructure.

Windows 11 Memory Changes for 8 GB PCs

Most of the work adjusts how Windows 11 handles memory on lower-specced hardware instead of adding features. Microsoft lists these changes:

  • Windows 11 keeps up to 2 GB more active data in memory before moving it to slower storage.
  • Windows connects directly to Microsoft Edge when the browser is already running in the background, which Microsoft says lets Edge launch up to 33 percent faster.
  • Microsoft Teams can enable Efficiency Mode by default on 8 GB machines, and the company says Teams then launches up to 20 percent faster.
  • Widgets load only when they are used instead of running all the time.
  • Edge puts inactive tabs to sleep after 15 minutes by default, down from two hours.

Third-party apps can use the same memory tweaks, according to Microsoft.

The blog post also cites benchmark data from research Microsoft commissioned, comparing 2026 Windows machines with models from 2021. In that report, a 2026 Dell XPS 13 with 8 GB of RAM performed about as well as a 2021 Dell XPS 13 with 16 GB across selected workloads. Microsoft's reading of the result is that "the complete PC, not memory capacity alone, shapes the experience."

Davuluri drew a line for heavier use as well. He described 8 GB as "a great fit for the things they do every day" for everyday users, while workloads such as 3D modeling, advanced video editing, or large-scale data processing "benefit from 16 GB of memory or more," according to the post.

How to Get the 8 GB Improvements on Windows 11

The gains depend on both the Windows 11 version and on app updates, so owners of 8 GB PCs need both parts current:

  1. Confirm the PC runs Windows 11 26H2, build 26300.9818 or later, and install pending updates through Windows Update.
  2. Update Microsoft apps such as Edge and Teams, since Microsoft says "some improvements arrive through app updates or through Microsoft Store."
  3. Review Edge tab behavior after updating. Tabs that sleep after 15 minutes free memory sooner but need to reload when reopened.

The 20 and 40 percent figures are Microsoft's own claims, and the commissioned benchmark covers selected workloads only. Microsoft has not said whether PCs on Windows 11 versions older than 26H2 will receive the same memory changes.

item.title: Rockstar Confirms GTA 6 Preload Starts November 10 With a Download of Up to 212 GB (2026)
item.description:
Rockstar Games has confirmed that digital preloading for Grand Theft Auto VI begins on Tuesday, November 10, and that the preload file requires up to 212 GB "depending on your device," according to a post on the Rockstar Newswire. GTA 6 launches globally on November 19 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S.

The PS5 date is earlier than some buyers expected. Pre-order forms had listed November 12 as the preload start, and Rockstar has now clarified that digital preloading on PS5 opens at midnight local time on November 10. Code-in-box versions for both consoles "should" be available from retailers beginning November 12, Rockstar says.

GTA 6 Preload and Launch Times on PS5 and Xbox

The two consoles follow different schedules. PS5 preloading starts at local midnight in each time zone, while Xbox Series X and S preloading opens at the same moment worldwide, 12 a.m. GMT on November 10. In the US, that puts the Xbox preload at 4 p.m. PT and 7 p.m. ET on November 9.

  • PS5 preload: 12 a.m. local time on November 10, which is 9 p.m. PST on November 9 in Los Angeles
  • Xbox Series X and S preload: 12 a.m. GMT on November 10, which is 8 a.m. in Beijing, 9 a.m. in Tokyo and Seoul, and 11 a.m. AEST in Melbourne
  • Launch on both platforms: midnight local time on November 19, which is 9 p.m. PST on November 18 in Los Angeles

Earlier PlayStation Store data had put the PS5 download at 210 GB. Rockstar's figure of up to 212 GB covers the preload file, PS5 and Xbox sizes may differ slightly, and final install sizes can differ from preload downloads. "So make sure you've got ample space to begin pre-loading as soon as possible," Rockstar said.

Players who want to start on launch night should prepare before November 10:

  1. Free up at least 212 GB of storage on the console before preloading opens.
  2. Note the preload start for the platform, local midnight on PS5 or 12 a.m. GMT on Xbox Series X and S.
  3. Expect codes for code-in-box physical editions from retailers from November 12, two days after digital preloading begins.

GTA 6 Cover Art Poster and Map of Leonida

Rockstar will add a printable GTA 6 cover art poster and map of Leonida as a free digital download on its official site on November 19. A double-sided physical version will follow shortly after launch on the Rockstar Store, priced at $0.99 on its own or free with any purchase from the store.

Rockstar has published a preload FAQ on its support site, but the publisher has not listed separate final install sizes for PS5 and Xbox Series X and S.

Thank you for being a Ghacks reader. The post Rockstar Confirms GTA 6 Preload Starts November 10 With a Download of Up to 212 GB appeared first on gHacks.

item.title: Federal judge sends Zula Casino lawsuit back to Georgia state court (2026)
item.description:
Federal judge Clay D. Land sent Georgia Gambling Recovery LLC’s lawsuit against Zula Casino’s operator and two Blazesoft companies back to Georgia state court on November 3, 2026. His order grants the plaintiff’s request to return the case to the State Court of Muscogee County.

The case names Blazesoft Ltd., Blazegames, Inc. and SCPS LLC, which operates as Zula Casino. The defendants moved the action to the U.S. District Court for the Middle District of Georgia in June. The federal case carries the number 4:26-cv-00914-CDL. The docket identifies the defendants and removal date.

Why the arbitration agreement failed to establish federal jurisdiction

The companies relied on the New York Convention, an international agreement concerning arbitration agreements and foreign arbitral awards, to establish federal jurisdiction. Land found that Georgia Gambling Recovery had neither signed the arbitration agreement nor agreed to be bound by it. He also rejected the defendants’ argument that Georgia law allowed them to enforce the agreement against the company.

Georgia Gambling Recovery seeks relief under the state’s gambling-loss recovery statute. Land explained that its asserted right to relief arose from that statute, rather than a contract containing an arbitration clause. He concluded that the defendants had failed to establish federal jurisdiction and directed the clerk to remand the action. The November 3 order sets out his reasoning.

Why the VGW, Blitz and Dabble cases stayed in federal court

On October 28, Land had kept the same plaintiff’s separate cases against VGW, Blitz Studios and Dabble in federal court. Those cases involved diversity jurisdiction, which depends on the parties’ citizenship and the amount in dispute. The court found those requirements satisfied. The Blazesoft case relied on a different jurisdictional basis through the arbitration convention. The October 28 order covers those three cases.

The November 3 ruling places the gambling-loss claim back before the State Court of Muscogee County for further proceedings on the underlying allegations.

item.title: Microsoft Upgrades Outlook Search With Seven Ranked Results and a Small Language Model Ranker (2026)
item.description:
Microsoft has introduced a revamped search experience in Outlook that shows seven ranked results instead of three and handles common stop words better, according to a Microsoft blog post. The new ranking layout is available across Outlook versions, including the new Outlook and Classic Outlook.

The redesign targets a long-standing problem with Outlook search: irrelevant emails show up in the results while the message a user actually needs is missing. Microsoft says it focused on three areas while building the new search, namely better ranking, improved performance when connectivity is poor, and a tighter feedback loop.

How the New Outlook Search Ranks Emails

A search in Outlook now lists seven ranked emails at the top rather than three. Microsoft ranks these messages by recency, sender, how much the message has been interacted with, and other signals. Showing more ranked messages is meant to surface the relevant email more often, and the larger set also helps Microsoft improve its ranking systems over time.

Stop words get different treatment as well. Words such as "the," "and," and "is" used to pull unrelated emails into the results, which users then had to scroll through in chronological order. Microsoft illustrates the change in its blog post with a search for "the FY27 budget," comparing what the old and the new Outlook search return for the same query.

The ranking comes from a small language model built specifically for Outlook. Microsoft trained it through distillation, a method in which a smaller model is built under the supervision of a larger one. That keeps search lightweight, because Outlook does not need to run a large model each time it ranks emails.

Classic Outlook Gets Offline Fallback and Faster Results First

Classic Outlook now falls back automatically to locally indexed content when the connection is poor, so searches still return results from mail stored on the device.

The same fallback is coming to the new Outlook, but Microsoft says it will ship later. Classic Outlook users should also see faster search results, and the company states that recent improvements reduced latency for the slowest 5% of Outlook searches.

Users can verify the changes in their own mailbox:

  1. Run a search that includes common words, for example a phrase that starts with "the," and check whether unrelated emails still appear at the top.
  2. Look for seven ranked emails above the regular results instead of three.
  3. In Classic Outlook, run a search on a slow or unstable connection to confirm that locally indexed results still appear.

Microsoft lists the tighter feedback loop as one of the three goals of the redesign and is asking Outlook users for feedback on the new results. No release date has been given for the local index fallback in the new Outlook.

item.title: Apple Will Check Public iCloud Share Links for Harmful Content Starting With iOS 27.3 (2026)
item.description:
Apple will start checking iCloud content shared through public links for "harmful content" with version 27.3 of iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and visionOS, according to a new Apple support page published on Tuesday. The checks apply only to items shared with the "Anyone with the Link" option, not to content shared directly with specific people.

The 27.3 releases went out to developers in beta on Tuesday, and a general release is expected in December. Apple has not said whether the checks are already active in the beta builds.

The policy reaches iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple Vision Pro users at the same version number, so anyone who creates public iCloud links on those devices is covered once the 27.3 updates are installed.

Apple's New Rules for Anyone With the Link Sharing in iCloud

"Items shared using Anyone with the Link will be checked by Apple for harmful content," the support page states. Apple does not define harmful content on the page. The company also has not explained how the checks work, or whether human moderators, automated systems, or both will identify and remove content.

Apple says it can access items shared this way. The public sharing option removes end-to-end encryption from the shared item, even when Advanced Data Protection, Apple's optional end-to-end encryption feature for supported iCloud data, remains enabled on the account.

When harmful content is found, Apple reserves the right to move, refuse, modify, remove, or delete it at any time, according to the support page. The company says it may also block or disable accounts associated with that content and reserves the right to involve law enforcement when necessary. Apple does not list which content types fall under the policy.

How iCloud Users Can Review Their Public Links

The checks are tied to the sharing method, not to iCloud storage as a whole. iCloud users who rely on public links can review their sharing habits before the 27.3 updates reach their devices:

  1. Go through iCloud items that are currently shared with Anyone with the Link and decide whether each link still needs to be public.
  2. Share sensitive items directly with specific people instead of creating a public link, since the checks cover only links that anyone can open.
  3. Keep in mind that Advanced Data Protection does not protect items shared with Anyone with the Link, because that option removes end-to-end encryption from the shared item.

The support page ties the checks to Anyone with the Link sharing only. Apple has not said whether items that were shared publicly before iOS 27.3 will also be checked once the update is installed, and the company has not given an exact release date beyond the expected December rollout.

item.title: Google Will Turn Gemini Gems Into Skills on November 17 and Remove the Old Gems on December 17 (2026)
item.description:
Google will replace Gems in Gemini with skills on November 17, 2026, for personal Google accounts of users aged 18 and older, and the original Gems will be removed from those accounts on December 17, according to Google. The company says it will migrate existing Gems automatically, but files attached to Gems face new limits and some file types will be deleted.

On November 17, Gems transition to skills. The original Gems stay visible for reference, but users can no longer use, edit, or create them. On December 17, Gems disappear from the account entirely.

Skills work differently from Gems. A Gem has to be opened directly, while a skill can be called up anywhere in Gemini, including in the middle of an existing chat, by typing a slash followed by the skill name.

Google plans to switch that trigger to the at sign. Skills can also run automatically based on a "When to use" section in their instructions, multiple skills can be stacked in one chat, and skills are built on the open SKILL.md standard, which makes them transferable to other AI platforms such as Claude and ChatGPT.

Gemini Gems Transition Timeline by Account Type

Google Workspace accounts follow a later schedule. For those users, Gems move into the Settings panel on November 17 but keep working until at least March 1, 2027. Education users will not see their Gems removed before June 1, 2027. Google has not announced when the transition starts for users under 18, and it has delayed the rollout of skills to Workspace apps such as Docs, Sheets, Slides, and Studio without a new date.

Skills come with restrictions. They do not work with Canvas, Deep Research, Guided Learning, video creation, or music creation. Content from Google Drive and Gemini Notebook cannot be added, skills cannot be shared with other users, and only 100 skills can be active at one time. Files added to a skill are capped at 100 MB, and skills do not sync between the Gemini app and Workspace apps.

How to Move Gems With Knowledge Files Before December 17

Simple, text-based Gems should survive the automatic migration. Gems with knowledge files need more attention: Google will delete the largest files to bring a skill under the 100 MB limit, and unsupported files are dropped, including legacy Office formats (.doc, .xls, .ppt), compressed archives, GitHub files, and audio and video files. Those files are deleted on December 17, so users should download them first.

  1. Click Gems in the Gemini sidebar, then click the Edit (pencil) button next to the Gem.
  2. Download every file listed under the Knowledge heading.
  3. Open a new Gemini tab and go to Customize, Skills, Create, and select Create manually.
  4. Paste the Gem's name, description, and instructions into the new skill and click Create.
  5. Edit the skill and use Add files for a small number of files, or download the skill, place its SKILL.md file in a folder with the knowledge files, and upload that folder with Replace skill.

Google has not set final removal dates for Workspace accounts, and no date has been announced for skills in Docs, Sheets, Slides, and Studio.

Thank you for being a Ghacks reader. The post Google Will Turn Gemini Gems Into Skills on November 17 and Remove the Old Gems on December 17 appeared first on gHacks.

item.title: Epic Games Raises Fortnite Crew to Up to 1,600 V-Bucks a Month From December 5 and Ends Monthly Skins (2026)
item.description:
Epic Games is changing the Fortnite Crew subscription on December 5, raising the base monthly V-Bucks grant back to 1,000 and adding higher amounts for long-term subscribers, according to a post on the official Fortnite blog. The price of Fortnite Crew stays the same, but the monthly Crew skin, one of the subscription's main perks, ends after December.

Fortnite Crew paid 1,000 V-Bucks per month for most of its existence. Earlier this year, Epic cut the grant to 800 following its V-Bucks price increases.

Fortnite Crew V-Bucks Tiers and New XP Bonus

From December 5, the monthly V-Bucks amount depends on how long a player has been subscribed without a break:

  • 1,000 V-Bucks per month as the new base amount
  • 1,200 V-Bucks per month after at least 3 consecutive months
  • 1,400 V-Bucks per month after 6 consecutive months
  • 1,600 V-Bucks per month from 12 months onward, the maximum

At the top level, a long-term subscriber receives twice the 800 V-Bucks that Crew paid after this year's cut. Epic assigns the tiers automatically to current subscribers on December 5.

Current subscribers will be placed in a bronze, silver, or gold tier based on the number of consecutive months they have been subscribed in the last year as of December 5. Lapsed subscribers who resubscribe between December 5 and December 31 get a starting tier based on their most recent continuous subscription period over the past 12 months, Epic says.

Former subscribers who want their past subscription history to count toward a higher starting tier need to resubscribe between December 5 and December 31. Epic has not said whether earlier Crew skins will ever be sold in the Item Shop once the monthly skins end.

item.title: Nintendo Sold 6.49 Million Switch 2 Consoles in Six Months, Down From 10.36 Million a Year Earlier (2026)
item.description:
Nintendo sold 6.49 million Switch 2 consoles between April 1 and September 30, 2026, down from 10.36 million in the same period a year earlier, according to the company's latest financial results.

The drop of 3.87 million units, roughly 37 percent, covers the first half of Nintendo's fiscal year and mostly predates the gaming console's $50 price increase in the US, Canada, and Europe.

Nintendo also lowered its expectations for the full year. The company now forecasts 16.5 million Switch 2 units sold by March 31, 2027, compared with 19.86 million in the previous 12-month period, a reduction of 16.9 percent.

Nintendo Switch 2 Hardware and Software Sales

Nintendo labels the reporting window FY27 Q1 to Q2, the first six months of its fiscal year ending March 31, 2027. The original Switch sold 1.27 million units in the same six months, down 32.7 percent. That decline is expected for a console in its final years.

The Switch 2 numbers stand out because the console's first year went so well. It sold 19.8 million units in that period, which is more than the original Switch managed in its first full year (around 17.7 million). The original Switch then doubled that figure in its second year, a pattern the Switch 2 forecast does not follow.

Software sales moved in the other direction:

  • Switch 2 games rose 18.8 percent, from 20.62 million to 24.49 million units
  • Switch games rose 6.8 percent, from 61.56 million to 65.73 million units

Nintendo says in its report that consumers continued to adopt the Switch 2 even though hardware sales declined year over year, and it credits the release of new titles for that.

Switch 2 Price Increase and the Holiday Quarter

Nintendo announced the Switch 2 price increase in May 2026. Japan saw the higher price immediately, while the US, Canada, and Europe moved to the new price on September 1, 2026. The console now costs $500, up from its $450 launch price. Nintendo attributed the change to "changes in market conditions."

Because the reporting period ended on September 30, the results show only one month of sales at the higher price in most Western markets. The reduced forecast is Nintendo's first indication of how it expects the holiday quarter to go.

For buyers, the current situation is straightforward. The Switch 2 costs $500 in the US, and Nintendo's sales growth now comes from software, including new releases such as the remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, which launched this week.

Nintendo has not broken down how much of the hardware decline it attributes to the price increase, and the effect of the $500 price on holiday sales will only show up in the company's next quarterly results.

item.title: Microsoft Will Add Opt-In Copilot Answers to the New Windows 11 Search Later This Year (2026)
item.description:
Microsoft will add an optional Copilot integration to the rebuilt Search experience in Windows 11, with the feature starting to roll out to select markets later this year, the company says. Microsoft states that the Copilot option will be opt-in, which means Windows 11 users who do not turn it on will not see Copilot inside the taskbar Search interface.

The announcement follows the overhauled Windows Search that Microsoft introduced in October. Microsoft says the new Search will begin rolling out before the end of 2026.

Copilot Integration in the New Windows 11 Search

Microsoft describes the integration in a short statement: "We will also begin adding the option to integrate the new Copilot with Search on the taskbar, so you can get quick answers inline from Search, and if you want to have a richer conversation, you can jump from Search directly to the full Copilot app." The company adds that "this experience will be opt-in, and will first start rolling out to select markets later this year."

Two modes are planned once the option is enabled:

  • quick Copilot answers shown inline in the taskbar Search results
  • a direct handoff from Search to the full Copilot app for longer conversations

The rebuilt Windows Search itself was designed from the ground up. Microsoft says it returns more accurate file and app results and can change settings or start actions that the user asks for. Users can also answer text messages, open apps, and preview images, files, and rich content without leaving the Search interface. The new version uses less web content and relies on native Windows UI frameworks, which Microsoft says makes the interface faster.

Why the Opt-In Model Matters for Windows 11 Users

The new Search builds on Ask Copilot, an experience Microsoft announced last year that never shipped outside of preview builds. Testing of Ask Copilot was paused over the summer. The new Windows Search looks almost identical to it.

One difference is control. Ask Copilot had no option to turn off the Copilot integration in its interface. The new Windows Search keeps the same design but makes Copilot a choice rather than a fixed part of the experience. Earlier this year, Microsoft also said it would reduce the amount of Copilot integration across Windows.

For users, the practical result is simple. Anyone who does not want AI answers in taskbar Search does not have to change anything, because the integration stays off unless it is turned on. Users who want Copilot answers in Search will have to wait until the option reaches their market and then enable it.

Microsoft has not listed the select markets that get the Copilot option first, and the company has not said where the opt-in setting will appear in Windows 11 or when it will reach additional languages and regions.
